purpose: Describe the small Google tag used on Mythical’s public shop window. The tag is not part of the game. It starts with analytics and advertising storage turned off, asks visitors before enabling analytics, explicitly sends only narrow public-page, Play and Share events after an affirmative choice, turns advertising features off, and never receives a game save, creature name, account number, email, age, child detail, full query string, or user ID from Mythical. Google Analytics also creates basic service events after consent, and the property currently has optional enhanced measurement enabled; that wider setting is recorded as a governance gap, not silently described as minimal. A visitor can say no. The tag is checked in the page source, consent helper, public privacy page, production hosting policies and the signed-in Google property.

consentJourneyEvidence.transportLimitation: The clean automated Chrome profile could not execute the third-party Google tag script, matching the known Google Tag Manager block in the broad production smoke. The test therefore proves Mythical's visible choice, saved refusal and permission states, event-queue boundary, and game exclusion, but it does not prove that this particular test event reached Google. Earlier signed-in property evidence separately proves that the correct stream has received data.

productionEvidence.limitation: A fresh temporary browser profile replayed the public choice on 8 September 2026. It showed the choice, queued no event before a decision, retained No thanks across reload with no event, retained Allow analytics and queued only discovery_arrival, and loaded no Google tag or Google request inside the game. The test browser itself blocked the third-party Google script, so this run did not prove transport to Google. Earlier signed-in property inspection separately proved that the correct stream had received data. No export was used, enhanced measurement remains enabled, and no count may be called players, plays, conversion, retention, enjoyment or growth.

propertySideEvidence.interpretation: This proves the owned stream is receiving data. It does not prove five players or five independent visits: the single reported user and the current direct sessions may be Kevin or Codex checks. The scroll event proves optional enhanced measurement is broader than the intended narrow explicit event set.
